verses.zh: 那时，分封的王希律听见耶稣的名声，
verses.en: At that time Herod the tetrarch[NOTE:1] heard reports about Jesus,
notes: A tetrarch, a ruler with rank and authority lower than a king, ruled only with the approval of the Roman authorities. This was roughly equivalent to being governor of a region. Several times in the NT, Herod, tetrarch of Galilee, is called a king (Matt 14:9, Mark 6:14-29), reflecting popular usage rather than an official title.

verses.zh: 就对臣仆说：「这是施洗的约翰从死里复活，所以这些异能从他里面发出来。」
verses.en: and he said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead! And because of this, miraculous powers are at work in him.”

verses.zh: 起先，希律为他兄弟腓力的妻子希罗底的缘故，把约翰拿住，锁在监里。
verses.en: For Herod had arrested John, bound him,[NOTE:1] and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife,
notes: ‡ Most witnesses (א1 C D L N W Z Γ Δ Θ 0106 ƒ1, 13 33 565 579 1241 1424 M lat) read αὐτόν (auton, “him”) here as a way of clarifying the direct object; various significant witnesses lack the word, however (א* B 700 ff1 h q al). The original wording most likely lacked it, but it has been included here due to English style. NA28 includes the word in brackets, indicating reservations about its authenticity.

verses.zh: 因为约翰曾对他说：「你娶这妇人是不合理的。」
verses.en: because John had repeatedly told[NOTE:1] him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfect tense verb is here rendered with an iterative force.
This marriage of Herod to his brother Philip’s wife was a violation of OT law (Lev 18:16; 20:21). In addition, both Herod Antipas and Herodias had each left marriages to enter into this union.

verses.zh: 希律就想要杀他，只是怕百姓，因为他们以约翰为先知。
verses.en: Although[NOTE:1] Herod[NOTE:2] wanted to kill John,[NOTE:3] he feared the crowd because they accepted John as a prophet.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated.
Grk “he”; the referent (Herod) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “him” (also in the following phrase, Grk “accepted him”); in both cases the referent (John) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 到了希律的生日，希罗底的女儿在众人面前跳舞，使希律欢喜。
verses.en: But on Herod’s birthday, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod,

verses.zh: 希律就起誓，应许随她所求的给她。
verses.en: so much that he promised[NOTE:1] with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
notes: The Greek text reads here ὁμολογέω (homologeō); though normally translated “acknowledge, confess,” BDAG (708 s.v. 1) lists “assure, promise” for certain contexts such as here.

verses.zh: 女儿被母亲所使，就说：「请把施洗约翰的头放在盘子里，拿来给我。」
verses.en: Instructed by her mother, she said, “Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter.”

verses.zh: 王便忧愁，但因他所起的誓，又因同席的人，就吩咐给她；
verses.en: Although it grieved the king[NOTE:1] because of his oath and the dinner guests, he commanded it to be given.
notes: Herod was technically not a king, but this reflects popular usage. See the note on tetrarch in 14:1.tn Grk “and being grieved, the king commanded.”

verses.zh: 于是打发人去，在监里斩了约翰，
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he sent and had John beheaded in the prison.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.

verses.zh: 把头放在盘子里，拿来给了女子；女子拿去给她母亲。
verses.en: His[NOTE:1] head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
notes: Grk “And his”; the referent (John the Baptist) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 约翰的门徒来，把尸首领去埋葬了，就去告诉耶稣。
verses.en: Then John’s[NOTE:1] disciples came and took the body and buried it and went and told Jesus.
notes: Grk “his”; the referent (John) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then.”

verses.zh: 耶稣听见了，就上船从那里独自退到野地里去。众人听见，就从各城里步行跟随他。
verses.en: Now when Jesus heard this he went away from there privately in a boat[NOTE:1] to an isolated place. But when the crowd heard about it,[NOTE:2] they followed him on foot from the towns.[NOTE:3]
notes: See the note at Matt 4:21 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.
The word “it” is not in the Greek text but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context.
Or “cities.”

verses.zh: 耶稣出来，见有许多的人，就怜悯他们，治好了他们的病人。
verses.en: As he got out he saw the large crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.

verses.zh: 天将晚的时候，门徒进前来，说：「这是野地，时候已经过了，请叫众人散开，他们好往村子里去，自己买吃的。」
verses.en: When evening arrived, his disciples came to him saying, “This is an isolated place[NOTE:1] and the hour is already late. Send the crowds away so that they can go into the villages and buy food for themselves.”
notes: Or “a desert” (meaning a deserted or desolate area with sparse vegetation).

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「不用他们去，你们给他们吃吧！」
verses.en: But he[NOTE:1] replied, “They don’t need to go. You[NOTE:2] give them something to eat.”
notes: ‡ The majority of witnesses read ᾿Ιησοῦς (Iēsous, “Jesus”) here, perhaps to clarify the subject. Although only a few Greek mss, along with several versional witnesses (א* D Zvid 579 1424 e k sys,c,p sa bo), lack the name of Jesus, the omission does not seem to be either accidental or malicious and is therefore judged to be most likely the original reading. Nevertheless, a decision is difficult. NA28 has the word in brackets, indicating doubts as to its authenticity.
Here the pronoun ὑμεῖς (humeis) is used, making “you” in the translation emphatic.

verses.zh: 门徒说：「我们这里只有五个饼，两条鱼。」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] said to him, “We have here only five loaves and two fish.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「拿过来给我。」
verses.en: “Bring them here to me,” he replied.

verses.zh: 于是吩咐众人坐在草地上，就拿着这五个饼，两条鱼，望着天祝福，擘开饼，递给门徒，门徒又递给众人。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he instructed the crowds to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and two fish, and looking up to heaven he gave thanks and broke the loaves. He gave them to the disciples,[NOTE:2] who in turn gave them to the crowds.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “Then.”

Grk “And after instructing the crowds to recline for a meal on the grass, after taking the five loaves and the two fish, after looking up to heaven, he gave thanks, and after breaking the loaves he gave them to the disciples.” Although most of the participles are undoubtedly attendant circumstance, there are but two indicative verbs—“he gave thanks” and “he gave.” The structure of the sentence thus seems to focus on these two actions and has been translated accordingly.
Grk “to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.”

verses.zh: 他们都吃，并且吃饱了；把剩下的零碎收拾起来，装满了十二个篮子。
verses.en: They all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up the broken pieces left over, 12 baskets full.

verses.zh: 吃的人，除了妇女孩子，约有五千。
verses.en: Not counting women and children, there were about 5,000 men who ate.

verses.zh: 耶稣随即催门徒上船，先渡到那边去，等他叫众人散开。
verses.en: Immediately Jesus[NOTE:1] made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he dispersed the crowds.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 散了众人以后，他就独自上山去祷告。到了晚上，只有他一人在那里。
verses.en: And after he sent the crowds away, he went up the mountain by himself to pray. When evening came, he was there alone.

verses.zh: 那时船在海中，因风不顺，被浪摇撼。
verses.en: Meanwhile the boat, already far from land,[NOTE:1] was taking a beating from the waves because the wind was against it.
notes: Grk “The boat was already many stades from the land.” A stade (στάδιον, stadion) was a unit of distance about 607 feet (185 meters) long.

verses.zh: 夜里四更天，耶稣在海面上走，往门徒那里去。
verses.en: As the night was ending,[NOTE:1] Jesus came to them walking on the sea.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “In the fourth watch of the night,” that is, between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m.
Or “on the lake.”

verses.zh: 门徒看见他在海面上走，就惊慌了，说：「是个鬼怪！」便害怕，喊叫起来。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] the disciples saw him walking on the water[NOTE:2] they were terrified and said, “It’s a ghost!” and cried out with fear.
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “on the sea”; or “on the lake.” The translation “water” has been used here for stylistic reasons (cf. the same phrase in v. 25).

verses.zh: 耶稣连忙对他们说：「你们放心，是我，不要怕！」
verses.en: But immediately Jesus[NOTE:1] spoke to them:[NOTE:2] “Have courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
notes: Most witnesses have ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς (ho Iēsous, “Jesus”), while a few lack the words (א* D 073 892 ff1 syc sa bo). Although such additions are often suspect (due to liturgical influences, piety, or for the sake of clarity), in this case it is likely that ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς dropped out accidentally. Apart from a few albeit significant witnesses, as noted above, the rest of the tradition has either ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς αὐτοῖς (ho Iēsous autois) or αὐτοῖς ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς (autois ho Iēsous). In majuscule letters, with Jesus’ name as a nomen sacrum, this would have been written as autoisois_ or ois_autois. Thus homoioteleuton could explain the reason for the omission of Jesus’ name. (This same phenomenon occurs in P137 at Mark 1:17 where the original text no doubt read αὐτοῖς ὁ ᾿Ιησοῦς, but this papyrus accidentally omits the nomen sacrum.)
Grk “he said to them, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 彼得说：「主，如果是你，请叫我从水面上走到你那里去。」
verses.en: Peter[NOTE:1] said to him,[NOTE:2] “Lord, if it is you, order me to come to you on the water.”
notes: Here δέ (de) has not been translated.
Grk “answering him, Peter said.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你来吧。」彼得就从船上下去，在水面上走，要到耶稣那里去；
verses.en: So he said, “Come.” Peter got out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.

verses.zh: 只因见风甚大，就害怕，将要沉下去，便喊着说：「主啊，救我！」
verses.en: But when he saw the strong wind he became afraid. And starting to sink, he cried out,[NOTE:1] “Lord, save me!”
notes: Grk “he cried out, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣赶紧伸手拉住他，说：「你这小信的人哪，为甚么疑惑呢？」
verses.en: Immediately Jesus reached out his hand and caught him, saying to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”

verses.zh: 他们上了船，风就住了。
verses.en: When they went up into the boat, the wind ceased.

verses.zh: 在船上的人都拜他，说：「你真是　神的儿子了。」
verses.en: Then those who were in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are the Son of God.”

verses.zh: 他们过了海，来到革尼撒勒地方。
verses.en: After they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.[NOTE:1]
notes: Gennesaret was a fertile plain south of Capernaum (see also Mark 6:53). The Sea of Galilee was also sometimes known as the Sea of Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

verses.zh: 那里的人一认出是耶稣，就打发人到周围地方去，把所有的病人带到他那里，
verses.en: When the people[NOTE:1] there recognized him, they sent word into all the surrounding area, and they brought all their sick to him.
notes: Grk “men”; the word here (ἀνήρ, anēr) usually indicates males or husbands, but occasionally is used in a generic sense of people in general, as here (cf. BDAG 79 s.v. 1.a, 2).

verses.zh: 只求耶稣准他们摸他的衣裳繸子；摸着的人就都好了。
verses.en: They begged him if[NOTE:1] they could only touch the edge of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.
notes: Grk “asked that they might touch.”
